content: I am large, I contain multitudes.
author: Walt Whitman
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Most human unhappiness exists in two places that don't currently exist: the past, which cannot be changed, and the future, which hasn't happened yet. Meanwhile, the only life you will ever experience is slipping past unnoticed.

Across his life and work, Walt Whitman saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Presence is not a rare mystical achievement; it is simply having the courtesy to show up for your own life. When you anchor your awareness in the immediate room and task, the frantic anxieties of the ego dissolve.
reflectionPrompt: Take a conscious breath right now: how much of your current stress exists only in your anticipation of tomorrow?
